mainTopic: The crow slaughtered for practice, whether רבי שמעון forbids a פטר חמור after its neck is broken, and the minimum value for redeeming it
overview: The גמרא first finishes its discussion of a פטר חמור slaughtered only for practice. It compares the case to an argument between נימוס and רבי אליעזר about a crow, and then suggests the crow may be special because it has kosher signs. Next it challenges רבה's view that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after its neck is broken (עריפה). The challenge comes from a ברייתא, which the גמרא answers by saying both clauses deal with a live donkey: one with benefit from its value and one with benefit from its body. רב נחמן brings two proofs that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after עריפה. Both proofs are pushed away. ריש לקיש agrees with רב נחמן, while רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר) says the dispute continues even after death. Another version applies the question to the משנה in קידושין about betrothing with a פטר חמור. רב explains that משנה using רבי יוסי בר יהודה's rule that redemption needs at least a שקל. Finally, the גמרא examines the source for that minimum, and it begins to explain how the רבנן read רבא's פסוק, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is slaughtering for practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier problem. The animal was slaughtered only to practice, and the argument matches the one between נימוס and רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? One where he slaughtered it to practice on it. The argument is the same as the one between נימוס and רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier difficulty by narrowing the case: the person slaughtered the donkey only to practice slaughtering, not to eat it. It then points us to an outside argument that will explain the disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal is slaughtered just for practice, nobody has shown any plan to eat it. So we must ask whether it still counts as food. The גמרא says this is the same question that נימוס and רבי אליעזר argued about, and it will now quote their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This phrase introduces a narrowed case.
To practice on it, to learn how to slaughter
An argument or dispute
A firstborn donkey, the subject of this discussion

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Such as where he slaughtered it to practice on it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the firstborn donkey the גמרא has been talking about.

phrases.english: and it is the argument of Nimos and Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised on the previous amud by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) and linking it to an existing argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case seemed to be an ordinary slaughter meant for eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a slaughter for practice, which depends on the argument of נימוס and רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a crow slaughtered for practice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reports that נימוס said the blood of a crow slaughtered for practice makes foods able to become impure. רבי אליעזר says the blood of slaughter always does so.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, נימוס, the brother of רבי יהושע הגרסי, told me that if someone slaughters a crow to practice on it, its blood makes foods ready to become impure. רבי אליעזר says the blood of slaughter always makes foods ready.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of the argument it just mentioned: a ברייתא about a crow slaughtered only for practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a food can become impure, it must first get wet from one of seven special liquids, and blood is one of them. This is called הכשר. נימוס says that even blood from a practice slaughter counts. רבי אליעזר says the blood of slaughter always counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He told me
A crow, which is a non-kosher bird
Makes a food ready to become impure, because blood is one of the seven liquids that do this
Blood that comes out during slaughter
Always

steps.confusionAlert: Here מַכְשִׁיר does not mean 'makes kosher.' It means 'makes a food able to become טמא.'

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
Nimos told me,
the brother of Rabbi Yehoshua HaGarsi,
that one who slaughters a crow to practice on it —
its blood makes foods ready to become impure.
phrases.notes: Blood is one of the seven liquids that, once they wet a food, make that food able to become טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The blood of slaughter always makes foods ready.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the argument mentioned in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נימוס: the blood of a crow slaughtered for practice is מכשיר. רבי אליעזר: the blood of slaughter is always מכשיר.

steps.title: The two opinions seem identical
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי אליעזר seems to say exactly what the תנא קמא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: both opinions say the blood makes foods ready, so what are they arguing about? This sets up the next step, where the גמרא finds the real difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נימוס, who is the first opinion, says the blood is מכשיר. רבי אליעזר also says the blood of slaughter is מכשיר. Two opinions should not be recorded as an argument if they say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
The first opinion in a ברייתא or משנה; here it is נימוס

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two opinions in the ברייתא of נימוס and רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions rule that the blood is מכשיר, so there seems to be no argument at all.

steps.title: They argue about whether being forbidden counts as intent
steps.stepSummary: The real argument is about איסורו חישובו: whether the crow's being forbidden counts as thinking of it as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that they argue about whether its being forbidden counts as having intent for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The two opinions do not argue about the blood. They argue about the crow's body: does the fact that a crow is forbidden count as treating it as food?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is not normally eaten counts as food only if a person has מחשבה, real intent to eat it. One opinion holds that its being forbidden already gives it the importance of food. The other opinion holds that real intent is still needed. This is exactly the question in Step 1's donkey slaughtered for practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? This phrase introduces the suggested real difference.
Its being forbidden counts as having intent for it as food
The difference between them is...

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the argument fits the donkey slaughtered for practice: the donkey is also forbidden, and nobody had intent to eat it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that
'its prohibition is its intent' is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means: does the fact that the crow is forbidden to eat count as if someone planned to eat it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו אִיסּוּרוֹ חִישּׁוּבוֹ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a hidden point of disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions seemed to say only that the blood is מכשיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about whether איסורו חישובו applies to the crow itself.

steps.title: The first opinion: blood counts, but the crow needs intent
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that the crow's blood makes other foods ready, but the crow itself counts as food only with real intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds that the crow's blood makes foods in general ready to become impure, but for the crow itself to count as food, intent is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the view of the תנא קמא (נימוס) under its new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the blood works on its own, so it makes other foods ready no matter what. The crow's body is a different matter. Since people do not usually eat crows, it is not food until someone has real intent to eat it, and its being forbidden is not enough. By implication, רבי אליעזר holds that איסורו חישובו, so the crow counts as food even without intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds, is of the opinion
For everything else, for other foods in general
For itself, for the crow's own body
Intent, here intent to use it as food

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא splits the crow in two. Its blood is always מכשיר, but its body becomes food only with מחשבה. The argument with רבי אליעזר is about whether איסורו חישובו, and this same question decides the case of the donkey slaughtered for practice.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
its blood makes other things ready to become impure,
but for itself, it needs intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the answer of Step 4 by explaining the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining one side of the argument
steps.terutzMaskana: For the תנא קמא, the blood is מכשיר for other foods, but the crow's body needs מחשבה, because its being forbidden does not count as intent.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's side of the argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 5 by explaining רבי אליעזר's view. Blood of slaughter always makes foods ready, and even the crow itself needs no special intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר comes to say: the blood of slaughter always makes foods able to become impure, and even for the crow itself, no intent is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its explanation of the argument. Step 5 explained the תנא קמא, and now it explains רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר goes further than the תנא קמא. The blood makes foods ready, and the crow's own meat also counts as food without any real intent. This is because he holds איסורו חישובו: the fact that the crow is forbidden counts as thinking of it as food.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood that comes out when an animal is slaughtered
Makes foods able to become impure (טומאת אוכלין)
For itself, meaning the crow's own meat
Intent or plan to use something as food

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
the blood of slaughter always makes [foods] susceptible [to impurity],
and even for [the crow] itself, too,
intent is not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation that began in Step 5 with the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר seemed to say the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר adds that the crow itself counts as food without intent, because its being forbidden counts as intent.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says the blood makes other foods ready, but the crow itself needs real intent. רבי אליעזר says even the crow itself needs no intent.

steps.title: Maybe the crow is special because it has kosher signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the comparison to the donkey case. Maybe רבי אליעזר's reason is that a crow has some kosher signs, so it does not teach anything about a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Maybe רבי אליעזר's reason there is that a crow is different, since it has some signs of a kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on linking the crow argument to the donkey argument. It offers another reason for רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the donkey argument matches the crow argument, both about איסורו חישובו. Now it suggests רבי אליעזר may only call the crow food because it has סימני טהרה. A donkey has no kosher signs, so the comparison could fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Perhaps, maybe
Is different
Crow or raven
Signs of a kosher animal or bird

phrases.english: From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps the reason of Rabbi Eliezer there
is that a crow is different,
since it has signs of a kosher [bird].

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the link between the crow argument and the donkey argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the donkey argument matches the argument between נימוס and רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's reason may be the crow's סימני טהרה, which a donkey does not have, rather than איסורו חישובו.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a crow is kosher. It is only saying a crow has some kosher signs, and that may be enough to make it count as food.

steps.title: Proof that kosher signs matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון explains that certain non-kosher animals count as food because they have some kosher signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that kosher signs make a real difference? Because a ברייתא teaches about that משנה: רבי שמעון said, what is the reason? Because it has kosher signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new suggestion. It shows that kosher signs really can make something count as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about the earlier משנה on the camel, hare, rock-badger, and pig. There רבי שמעון explains that they count as food because they have some kosher signs. So it is reasonable that רבי אליעזר treats the crow as food for the same reason.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
It is a significant matter; it makes a real difference
It is taught about it (a ברייתא commenting on a משנה)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that kosher signs are a significant matter?
For it is taught about that [משנה],
phrases.notes: That earlier משנה about the camel, hare, rock-badger, and pig.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Because it has kosher signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of Step 7 by showing that kosher signs really matter.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that סימני טהרה can make a non-kosher creature count as food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the משנה about the camel, hare, rock-badger, and pig, where רבי שמעון gives this reason.

steps.title: Then why limit the case to practicing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a question about the new explanation. If kosher signs are the reason, the crow should count as food even if it was slaughtered without paying attention, so why talk about slaughtering for practice?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: if the reason is kosher signs, why speak specifically about slaughtering to practice? Even slaughtering without paying attention should work too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to the kosher-signs explanation, and the next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If kosher signs make the crow food, intent should not matter at all. Then רבי אליעזר should agree even when someone slaughtered the crow without paying attention. So why does the case mention slaughtering to practice?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible objection)
Why specifically this case?
To practice or teach oneself (how to slaughter)
To act without paying attention (מתעסק)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
if it is because of kosher signs,
why specifically [the case of slaughtering] to practice?
Even [slaughtering] without paying attention, too!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי מִשּׁוּם סִימָנֵי טׇהֳרָה, מַאי אִירְיָא לְהִתְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the kosher-signs explanation from Steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי אליעזר's reason is the crow's סימני טהרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If kosher signs alone make the crow food, the special case of slaughtering to practice seems unnecessary. Even slaughtering without paying attention should work.

steps.title: Yes, and the case was chosen because of נימוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that for רבי אליעזר even careless slaughter would work. The case of practicing was chosen only to show how far נימוס goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so, and the case was taught because of נימוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by agreeing with it. The detail of slaughtering to practice comes from נימוס, not רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, even slaughtering without paying attention would make the crow count as food. The case is about slaughtering to practice because נימוס says that even a deliberate slaughter, done only for practice, does not count. So the kosher-signs explanation stands, and the proof for the donkey case is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (agreeing with the question)
The Sage who argues with רבי אליעזר about the crow

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
and [the case was taught] because of Nimos.
phrases.notes: The case shows that נימוס says no even when the slaughter was on purpose, as long as it was only for practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 by agreeing with it and explaining why the case was chosen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreeing, then explaining the case choice (אין הכי נמי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning slaughter for practice seemed to show that רבי אליעזר needs it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר does not need it. The case was chosen to show how far נימוס goes.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא shows that the crow argument may be about סימני טהרה, not איסורו חישובו. So it does not clearly match the donkey argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: This weakens the earlier claim that the donkey argument is the same as the argument between נימוס and רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show רבי שמעון permits benefit after neck-breaking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה with a ברייתא. It says that after a פטר חמור has its neck broken, רבי יהודה forbids benefit, while רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objected: If the owner does not want to redeem his firstborn donkey, he breaks its neck from behind with a cleaver and buries it. It is forbidden to benefit from it, says רבי יהודה. But רבי שמעון permits it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבה's view. רבה said that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after its neck is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the donkey being killed and buried. Then it says רבי יהודה forbids benefit and רבי שמעון permits it. Read simply, רבי שמעון permits benefit from the dead donkey, which is the opposite of what רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a ברייתא
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb or else have its neck broken
Breaking the neck from behind, the Torah's way of killing an unredeemed פטר חמור
A cleaver, a heavy butcher's knife
A ban on getting any benefit or use from something

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the central question of the section: whether the איסור הנאה on a פטר חמור continues after the עריפה, according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, who said even רבי שמעון forbids benefit after the neck is broken.

phrases.english: If he did not want to redeem it,
he breaks its neck with a cleaver from behind and buries it,
and it is forbidden for benefit,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda;
and Rabbi Shimon permits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the crow discussion, the גמרא directly attacks רבה's position on the dead פטר חמור using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא places the dispute right after describing the עריפה and burial, so רבי שמעון seems to permit benefit from the dead donkey.

steps.title: Read the dispute as being about the live donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dispute in the ברייתא is about benefit while the donkey is still alive, not after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: While it is alive, it is forbidden for benefit, says רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by changing how we read the ברייתא. The argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון is about the living donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון only permits benefit while the donkey is alive, he may still agree that after the עריפה it is forbidden. That would fit רבה's view perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, meaning read the source this way instead
While still alive

phrases.english: Say:
and while it is alive it is forbidden for benefit,
and Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 11 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (the dispute is moved to the live animal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's dispute is about benefit after the עריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about benefit while alive, so רבי שמעון may forbid after the עריפה, as רבה said.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא is already about a live donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. The last part of the ברייתא already deals with the live donkey, so the first part must be about the dead one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last clause is about while it is alive, the first clause must not be about while it is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 12. The ברייתא would not discuss the live donkey twice, so the first clause must be about after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two separate disputes between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. The second one clearly deals with a live donkey. So the first one must be about something else, the donkey after its neck is broken, and the challenge to רבה comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, an opening word for a challenge
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two disputes. The first one, after the neck-breaking, is about benefit. The second one, about shearing and work, is about a live donkey. The גמרא's point is that they cannot both be about a live donkey.

phrases.english: But since the latter clause is about while it is alive,
the first clause is not about while it is alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rereading of Step 12 and brings back the objection of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the first clause is about the live donkey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause already covers the live donkey, so repeating that would be pointless. The first clause must refer to the dead donkey.

steps.title: Quoting the end of the ברייתא about shearing and work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last clause of the ברייתא. It forbids other ways of killing the donkey and records a dispute about shearing it and working with it, which only make sense while it is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the last clause teaches: He may not kill it with a reed, a sickle, an ax, or a saw. He may not put it in a room and lock the door so that it dies. Shearing it and working with it are forbidden, says רבי יהודה, and רבי שמעון permits!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim from Step 13 by quoting the end of the ברייתא. It shows that this part deals with the donkey while it is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only shear a donkey or make it work while it is alive. So the dispute in the last clause is clearly about a live donkey. That means the first dispute, the one right after the עריפה, must be about the dead donkey. Then רבי שמעון does permit benefit after death, against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: For it teaches
An ax
Shearing (cutting the hair or wool)
Labor, making the animal work

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has two disputes between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. The second (shearing and work) is about a live donkey. So the first (benefit after the עריפה) must be about a dead donkey, and רבה's view is challenged again.

phrases.english: For the latter clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְמִיתֶנּוּ, לֹא בְּקָנֶה וְלֹא בְּמַגָּל
phrases.english: He may not kill it, not with a reed nor with a sickle,
nor with an ax nor with a saw,
and he may not put it into a room
and lock the door in front of it so that it will die,
and it is forbidden for shearing and for work,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda;
and Rabbi Shimon permits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that proves the claim made in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the last clause of the ברייתא deals with a live donkey
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last clause of the ברייתא, which records a dispute about shearing and work, things that apply only to a living animal

steps.title: Both clauses deal with a live donkey, but with different kinds of benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא saves its answer by saying both clauses of the ברייתא deal with a live donkey. The first clause is about benefit from its value, and the second is about benefit from its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both the first part and the last part are talking about the donkey while it is alive. The first part is about benefit from its value, like selling or renting it. The last part is about benefit from the animal itself, like shearing it or working with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 13 by showing that the two clauses are not repeating each other. Each one is about a different kind of benefit from a live donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that if the last clause is about a live donkey, the first clause must be about a dead one. The גמרא answers that both are about a live donkey, but they teach different things: benefit from its value versus benefit from its body. That keeps the reading from Step 12, so the ברייתא never says רבי שמעון permits benefit after עריפה, and רבה's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a teaching
The last clause of a teaching
While it is still alive
Benefit from its value, such as selling or renting it out
Benefit from the animal's body itself, such as shearing it or working with it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of benefit. 'Value' means money you get through the animal, like selling or renting it. 'Body' means using the animal directly, like taking its wool or making it work.

phrases.english: The first clause and the last clause are both about while it is alive;
the first clause is about benefit from its value,
the last clause is about benefit from its body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Steps 13-14 and restores the answer from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: two different kinds of benefit while the donkey is alive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last clause covers the live donkey, so the first clause must be about the dead one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses are about a live donkey. One deals with benefit from its value and the other with benefit from its body.

steps.title: Why the dispute had to be taught for both kinds of benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed to record the dispute twice. From either case alone, we might have guessed that one side agrees in the other case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If the ברייתא had taught only benefit from its value, I would think רבי שמעון permits only there, but for benefit from its body he agrees with רבי יהודה that it is forbidden. And if it had taught only benefit from its body, I would think רבי יהודה forbids only there, but for benefit from its value he agrees with רבי שמעון. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud: why repeat the same argument twice? It shows that each case teaches something we could not learn from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Benefit from the body seems more serious, so רבי שמעון might have forbidden it. Benefit from the value seems lighter, so רבי יהודה might have allowed it. Teaching both cases shows that each רבי keeps his view in both, so there is no repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; each case teaches something new
If the ברייתא had taught only...
I might have said; a possible mistaken assumption
Agrees with the other opinion
Permits

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes the remaining weak spot in the reading from Step 15. Once both clauses have their own purpose, the ברייתא no longer challenges רבה.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if he had taught only benefit from its value,
I would say that in that case Rabbi Shimon permits,
but regarding benefit from its body,
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Yehuda that it is forbidden.
And if he had taught only benefit from its body,
I would say that in that case Rabbi Yehuda forbids,
but regarding benefit from its value,
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Shimon that it is permitted.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 15 by showing that the two clauses do not repeat each other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Teaching the dispute twice is pointless repetition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case is needed, because from either one alone we might think one side agrees in the other case.

steps.title: Another אמורא supports רבה: רבי שמעון forbids benefit after עריפה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says that רבי שמעון agrees that the donkey is forbidden after its neck is broken. This is the same view as רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: רבי שמעון agrees that after the neck is broken, the donkey is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the challenge is answered, the גמרא brings another אמורא who says the same thing as רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's lenient view applies only while the donkey is alive. After עריפה, everyone agrees that no benefit is allowed. This matches what רבה held, which is why the ברייתא in Step 11 at first looked like a challenge to him.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said; introduces support for an earlier view
Breaking the neck, done with a פטר חמור that was not redeemed
After

phrases.english: And similarly Rav Nachman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Rabbi Shimon agrees that after the neck is broken
it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge to רבה is answered, this step adds another אמורא who agrees with him.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit after עריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה

steps.title: The source: a גזירה שוה from עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן proves his view from a ברייתא. The word עריפה appears both by פטר חמור and by עגלה ערופה, so just as עגלה ערופה is forbidden, a פטר חמור whose neck was broken is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: the Torah says 'and you shall break its neck.' Breaking the neck is said here, and breaking the neck is said there, by עגלה ערופה. Just as there it is forbidden, so too here it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the source for what he said in Step 17. He compares the פטר חמור to the עגלה ערופה because the Torah uses the same word for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places teaches that the same law applies to both. Benefit from עגלה ערופה is forbidden, so benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה is also forbidden. The ברייתא does not name a תנא. The next step argues that it must follow רבי שמעון, and that is how it would prove רב נחמן's point.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? This asks for the source
And you shall break its neck (שמות י״ג:י״ג)
There, meaning in another place in the Torah
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, a פטר חמור may be used while alive, whether for its value or its body. רב נחמן claims that after its neck is broken even רבי שמעון forbids it, learning this from עגלה ערופה through the shared word עריפה. רב ששת challenges this proof in step 20, and רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר) disagrees in step 27.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב נחמן offers this as a Torah source for רבה's view that even רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after the neck is broken. Steps 19-20 test whether the ברייתא really follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
From where do I say this?
As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'And you shall break its neck.'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about a firstborn donkey that was not redeemed (שמות י״ג:י״ג).

phrases.english: Breaking the neck is said here,
and breaking the neck is said there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the עגלה ערופה in ספר דברים, פרק כ״א.

phrases.english: just as there it is forbidden,
so too here it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the statement in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That benefit from a פטר חמור is forbidden after עריפה, even according to רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns a גזירה שוה from the word עריפה, shared with עגלה ערופה

steps.title: The עריפה ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It cannot be רבי יהודה, who already forbids the donkey while it is alive. So it must be רבי שמעון, which supports רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this ברייתא? If you say רבי יהודה, he already forbids the donkey while it is alive! So isn't it רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's proof by showing that the ברייתא from the last step must follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit even while alive. So he does not need a special teaching that it is forbidden after its neck is broken. That teaching only adds something new for רבי שמעון, so the ברייתא must be his. That means רבי שמעון agrees the donkey is forbidden after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose view is this?
If you say
While it is still alive
Rather, isn't it...? (introduces the only remaining option)

phrases.english: Whose view is this? If you say it is Rabbi Yehuda,
he already forbids it while it is alive!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from step 18 by working out which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's claim that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after its neck is broken.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא linking פטר חמור to עגלה ערופה. Only for רבי שמעון does it teach something new.

steps.title: רב ששת: the ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes ספרא, who says the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It was still needed, because we might have thought breaking the neck takes the place of redemption and so permits the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to רב נחמן: Your colleague ספרא explained it this way. The ברייתא really follows רבי יהודה, and it was still needed. You might have thought that breaking the neck stands in place of redeeming. Just as redeeming permits the donkey, breaking the neck would also permit it. So the ברייתא teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects רב נחמן's proof. He shows the ברייתא can fit רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that the ברייתא adds nothing for רבי יהודה. רב ששת shows it does add something even for him. The פסוק offers breaking the neck as the alternative to redemption, and redemption permits the donkey, so we might have thought breaking the neck permits it too. The ברייתא rules that out, so it does not have to be רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the first option after all)
It was needed
You might have thought
Redemption of the פטר חמור with a lamb
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת does not say רבי שמעון permits the donkey after עריפה. He only says this ברייתא does not prove the point either way.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to him:
Safra, your colleague, explained it:
Actually it is Rabbi Yehuda, and it was needed,
because you might have thought:
breaking the neck stands in place of redemption,
just as redemption permits,
so too breaking the neck permits,
so it teaches us that it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: סָפְרָא חַבְרָיךְ תַּרְגּוּמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 19 by showing the ברייתא is needed even for רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject רב נחמן's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא was pointless for רבי יהודה. But it is needed to rule out the idea that breaking the neck permits the donkey the way redemption does.

steps.title: רב נחמן's second proof: לוי's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא taught by לוי: the owner caused the כהן to lose money, so the owner's own money must be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Where do I get this from? From what לוי teaches: He caused the כהן to lose money, so his own money shall be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a new source for his view. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the next step will show how it proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason the Torah requires breaking the neck. The owner did not redeem the donkey, so the כהן lost the lamb he should have received. As a fair penalty, the owner loses the value of his donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
Teaches (a ברייתא)
Caused a loss of his money

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From where do I say it?
From what Levi teaches:
He caused the priest to lose money,
therefore his own money shall be lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? מִדְּתָנֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his first proof was rejected, רב נחמן brings a second source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after its neck is broken.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's ברייתא: the owner caused a loss, so his money is lost.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view לוי's ברייתא follows. For רבי יהודה, the owner's money is already lost while the donkey is alive. So the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון's, and for him breaking the neck is what causes the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי יהודה, the money is already lost! So isn't it רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out which תנא follows לוי's ברייתא, and shows it supports רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the living donkey is already forbidden, so its value is already gone. Breaking its neck would not cause any new loss. Only for רבי שמעון, who permits the living donkey, does breaking the neck make the owner lose his money. That loss only happens if the dead donkey is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands already lost

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רב נחמן's proofs use the same method. For רבי יהודה, the donkey is already forbidden while alive. So any source that makes breaking the neck forbid the donkey must be teaching רבי שמעון's view.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? If you say it is Rabbi Yehuda,
it already stands lost!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — הָא מַיפְסַד וְקָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second proof by identifying the תנא of לוי's ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון holds that breaking the neck makes the donkey forbidden for benefit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's ברייתא. Its idea of a new loss only works for רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The ברייתא Could Fit Either תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the claim that לוי's ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון. It says the ברייתא can fit רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבי יהודה. And if you want, say it follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 22 by saying the ברייתא can work for either תנא. This line is a setup: the next two steps explain how each option works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 argued that only רבי שמעון could say the owner 'loses money' because of breaking the neck. Here the גמרא says both תנאים can explain that loss. If both can, the ברייתא proves nothing about רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one possible answer or explanation
A pushing-away of a proof

phrases.english: If you want, say it is רבי יהודה,
and if you want, say it is רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 22 that the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב נחמן's reading of רבי שמעון from לוי's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'loss of money' in the ברייתא can be explained under both תנאים, so it does not pin down רבי שמעון.

steps.title: How It Fits רבי יהודה: The Lost Difference
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יהודה, the owner's loss is the gap between the donkey's value and the cheap lamb he could have used to redeem it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי יהודה, and the loss means the difference between the donkey's value and the lamb's value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה can say the owner 'loses money' by breaking the neck, even though the donkey was already forbidden while alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the live donkey is forbidden, but the owner could have redeemed it with a lamb worth less and then kept the donkey. Breaking its neck takes away that chance. So he loses the difference between the donkey and the lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: A loss
In between: the gap between two values
Redemption: exchanging the פטר חמור for a lamb

phrases.english: If you want, say it is רבי יהודה,
and it refers to the loss of what is in between.
phrases.notes: 'In between' means the gap between what the donkey is worth and what the lamb costs. Redeeming would have saved him that gap.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אַפְּסֵידָא דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first option from step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי יהודה the owner has nothing left to lose, since the donkey is already forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: He does lose something: the chance to redeem cheaply and keep a valuable donkey.

steps.title: How It Fits רבי שמעון: A Dead Donkey Is Worth Less
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי שמעון, even if the dead donkey is permitted, the owner loses because a dead donkey is worth less than a live one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is רבי שמעון, and the loss is the drop in value caused by death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי שמעון can also fit the ברייתא, even if he permits benefit from the donkey after its neck is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 assumed the 'loss' must mean the donkey becomes forbidden. Here the loss is simply that killing the donkey lowers its value. So רבי שמעון can permit the carcass and still agree that the owner lost money.

keyTerms.meaning: A drop in value
Death

steps.whatToRemember: לוי's ברייתא works for both תנאים: for רבי יהודה the loss is the redemption gap, and for רבי שמעון it is the drop in value from death. So it cannot prove רב נחמן's view.

phrases.english: And if you want, say it is רבי שמעון,
and it refers to the drop in value from death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לִפְחַת מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second option from step 23, which completes the rejection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner's loss must mean the donkey becomes forbidden in benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loss can just be the lower value of a dead animal, even if it stays permitted.

steps.title: ריש לקיש Agrees with רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רבי שמעון agrees that a פטר חמור is forbidden after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said the same: רבי שמעון agrees that after the neck is broken, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the proofs were pushed away, the גמרא brings an אמורא who holds like רב נחמן's reading of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות did not prove the point, but ריש לקיש states it directly. In his view, רבי שמעון argues with רבי יהודה only about the live donkey. Once the neck is broken, both forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said: brings an אמורא who holds the same view
Agrees, admits
After the neck is broken

phrases.english: And so said ריש לקיש:
רבי שמעון agrees
that after the neck is broken it is forbidden,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was pushed away, brings an אמורא who backs רב נחמן's position.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון forbids a פטר חמור after its neck is broken

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The Dispute Continues After Death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר) says רבי שמעון still argues after the neck is broken and permits the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי אלעזר, said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite view. רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר) holds that the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון continues even after the donkey is killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, רבי שמעון permits benefit from the פטר חמור even after its neck is broken, and רבי יהודה still forbids it. So אמוראים disagree about what רבי שמעון holds after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say: some say the statement was said by someone else
Still
A dispute

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after its neck is broken. רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר): רבי שמעון still permits it, so the dispute continues.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Still a dispute' does not mean nobody knows the answer. It means רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה keep arguing even after the donkey dies.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֲמַר:
phrases.english: But רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי אלעזר, said:
It is still a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֲמַר: עֲדַיִין הִיא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש's view in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור even after its neck is broken; the dispute with רבי יהודה continues.

steps.title: Another version: רב נחמן's teaching was said on the משנה in קידושין
steps.stepSummary: Some place רב נחמן's teaching on the משנה that says a woman betrothed with a פטר חמור is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach this statement of רב נחמן on a different source: the משנה that says, 'One who betroths a woman with a פטר חמור, she is not betrothed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving רב נחמן's teaching to a different source, a משנה in קידושין. This is a setup line that brings in the משנה about to be discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says קידושין made with a פטר חמור does not work. That only makes sense if the donkey is forbidden for benefit, since you need something of value to betroth a woman. That point is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (on a different source)
One who betroths a woman
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
She is not betrothed

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אַהָא:
phrases.english: There are those who teach this statement of Rav Nachman on this:
'One who betroths a woman with a firstborn donkey,
she is not betrothed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of where the discussion about רבי שמעון and the broken neck took place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman betrothed with a פטר חמור is not betrothed.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה in קידושין does not follow רבי שמעון, who permits benefit from a פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether this משנה goes against רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a פטר חמור may be used for benefit. If so, it has value and should work for קידושין. Since the משנה says it does not work, it seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
Not following the view of

phrases.english: Shall we say that our Mishnah does not follow Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה that says betrothal with a פטר חמור fails
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור, so under his view the betrothal should work.

steps.title: The case is after the neck was broken, so everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the משנה speaks after עריפה, when even רבי שמעון forbids the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the משנה is talking about after the neck was broken, and then everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a donkey whose neck was already broken, so it fits every opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner has broken the donkey's neck (עריפה), even רבי שמעון agrees it is forbidden for benefit. So the betrothal fails for everyone, and the משנה does not go against רבי שמעון. This matches ריש לקיש's view from step 26.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the donkey's neck, done when the owner chooses not to redeem it
Everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
It is after the neck was broken, and everyone agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה goes against רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is after עריפה, when all agree the donkey is forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה seems to fit neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the גמרא asks: under רבי שמעון she should be betrothed with the full value, and under רבי יהודה with the difference in value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the question was: whose view is this? It is neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון! If it is רבי שמעון, she should be betrothed with the whole donkey's value. If it is רבי יהודה, she should be betrothed with the amount in between.
steps.whatsHappening: In a different version, the גמרא asks a stronger question: the משנה seems to fit no one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits the donkey, so it is fully worth money. רבי יהודה (step 24) says the owner keeps the gap between the donkey's value and a cheap lamb, so at least that gap is his and could betroth her. Either way something of value was given, so why does the משנה say she is not betrothed?

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (a different version of the discussion)
Whose view is this?
The amount in between, the difference in value

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as step 29. There the problem was only רבי שמעון; here the גמרא claims the משנה fits neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: There are those who say: whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Yehuda and not Rabbi Shimon.
If it is Rabbi Shimon, she should be betrothed with all of it,

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — תִּיקְדַּשׁ בְּהָךְ דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי!
phrases.english: if it is Rabbi Yehuda, she should be betrothed with that amount in between!
phrases.notes: This is the gap between the donkey's value and the lamb, which belongs to the owner, as in step 24.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first version's question with a broader one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה that says betrothal with a פטר חמור fails
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under each opinion the man gave her something of value: the whole donkey under רבי שמעון, or the leftover value under רבי יהודה.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, when the donkey is worth only a shekel
steps.stepSummary: רב: the משנה follows רבי יהודה, in a case where the donkey is worth just a שקל, and he agrees with רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה said in the name of רב: really it is רבי יהודה, in a case where the donkey is worth only a שקל, and he holds like רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the משנה is רבי יהודה, in a case where the donkey is worth only one שקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If redemption must be with at least a שקל's worth, and the donkey is worth only a שקל, there is no leftover value. The owner owns nothing extra, so he has nothing to betroth her with. That is why the betrothal fails even under רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really (keeping the original idea and explaining it)
For example, in a case where
A coin of set value, here the lowest allowed value for redemption

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh said in the name of Rav:
Really, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and it is a case where it is worth only a shekel,

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: and he holds like Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּכְגוֹן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה אֶלָּא שֶׁקֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case, plus adding a matching opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי יהודה there is always leftover value she could be betrothed with.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the donkey is worth just a שקל and redemption needs at least a שקל, nothing is left over.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says redemption needs at least a שקל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'תפדה' to redeem right away and for any amount; רבי יוסי בר יהודה says no less than a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall redeem,' 'you shall redeem': redeem right away, redeem with any amount. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: redemption is never for less than a שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that is the source for רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view, used in the previous answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion reads the word תפדה as allowing redemption with a lamb of any value. רבי יוסי בר יהודה disagrees and sets a minimum of a שקל. רב's answer only works with this minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches
You shall redeem
Right away
Any amount at all
Redemption

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יהודה together with רבי יוסי בר יהודה, a פטר חמור worth only a שקל leaves the owner with nothing, so it cannot be used for קידושין.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'You shall redeem,' 'You shall redeem':
redeem it right away, redeem it with any amount.
Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
There is no redemption for less than a shekel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the opinion just used.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי בר יהודה requires at least a שקל for redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding the word תפדה

steps.title: Why do we need a verse for this? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא and asks why a פסוק is needed to teach redeeming right away and for any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'You shall redeem,' 'you shall redeem': redeem right away, redeem with any amount. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks closely at the ברייתא it just quoted and asks why its teachings needed a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming right away and redeeming with any amount seem like things we would assume anyway. So why would the תורה need extra wording to teach them? The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting a source in order to examine it)
It is obvious! (why say it?)

phrases.english: The Master said: 'You shall redeem,' 'You shall redeem':
redeem it right away, redeem it with any amount.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from using the ברייתא to examining it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These rules seem obvious, so there is no need for a פסוק to teach them.

steps.title: The verse was needed so we would not copy the rules of a firstborn son
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תפדה' was needed. Without it, we might compare the פטר חמור to a בכור אדם and require waiting thirty days and paying five. The פסוק teaches: redeem right away, and for any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought that since the donkey is compared to a firstborn son, the donkey should work like the son. A firstborn son is redeemed after thirty days, with five coins. So the donkey too would be redeemed after thirty days, with five. So the פסוק teaches us: 'You shall redeem' means right away, and 'you shall redeem' means for any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 34. The extra word 'תפדה' is needed to stop a mistaken comparison to a בכור אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פטר חמור and the בכור אדם appear together in the same פסוק. That is a הקש, a comparison, and it could make us copy the son's rules: wait thirty days, and give five סלעים. The repeated 'תפדה' blocks this. The donkey is redeemed immediately and for any value.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary; the source is not extra after all
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
It is compared to (by being placed next to it in the פסוק)
A firstborn son, who is redeemed from a כהן
So it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: 'שלשים וחמש' does not mean the number thirty-five. It means two separate things: after thirty days, and with five סלעים.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
for it would enter your mind to say:
since it is compared to a firstborn son,

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר אָדָם אַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ,
phrases.english: just as a firstborn son is after thirty and with five,
phrases.notes: Thirty means thirty days old. Five means five סלעים given to the כהן.

phrases.english: this donkey too would be after thirty days and with five.
So it teaches us:
'You shall redeem' means immediately,
'You shall redeem' means for any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34 about why a פסוק was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the פסוק is needed to block a mistaken הקש to בכור אדם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the הקש, the פטר חמור would be redeemed only after thirty days and for five סלעים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תפדה' teaches the donkey is redeemed immediately and for any amount.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי בר יהודה get his minimum of a שקל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who says redemption must be at least a שקל. Either way this is hard to explain. With the comparison to a firstborn son he should need five. Without it, where does a שקל come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: there is no redemption for less than a שקל. Either way you look at it, there is a problem. If he compares the donkey to a firstborn son, he should require five. And if he does not compare them, where does he get a שקל from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the second half of the ברייתא from step 33. It challenges רבי יוסי בר יהודה with a two-sided 'either way' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שקל is a middle amount, and that is the problem. The הקש to בכור אדם would give five סלעים. With no הקש, there would be no minimum at all, which is the 'any amount' view. So the גמרא wants a source for exactly a שקל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you take it; an either-way challenge
He compares (applies the הקש)
Redemption
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
There is no redemption for less than a shekel.
Whichever way you look at it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי מַקֵּישׁ לִבְכוֹר אָדָם — חָמֵשׁ לִיבְעֵי,
phrases.english: if he compares it to a firstborn son, he should require five,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא מַקֵּישׁ — שֶׁקֶל מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and if he does not compare them, from where does he get a shekel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first view in the ברייתא (any amount) to רבי יוסי בר יהודה's minimum.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר יהודה's ruling that redemption must be at least a שקל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With the הקש the amount should be five. Without the הקש there is no source for any minimum. A שקל fits neither option.

steps.title: No comparison: the שקל comes from the rule of valuations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה does not use the comparison to a firstborn son. He learns the שקל from רבא's teaching: 'all your valuations shall be with the שקל הקודש'. That means no valuation may be less than a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does not compare them. רבא said: the פסוק says, 'And all your valuations shall be with the shekel of the Sanctuary.' This means every valuation you make should not be less than a shekel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 36. רבי יוסי בר יהודה does not use the הקש. His שקל comes from a different פסוק that sets a minimum for valuations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'either way' challenge is solved by taking the second option: no הקש. The minimum is not borrowed from בכור אדם. It comes from a general rule: anything we value for holy purposes must be worth at least a שקל.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually; really (keeping one side of the earlier choice)
The פסוק says
Valuations (amounts set for holy purposes)
The holy shekel, the Torah's standard coin

steps.whatToRemember: The first view in the ברייתא learns from 'תפדה' that a פטר חמור is redeemed right away and for any amount. רבי יוסי בר יהודה requires at least a שקל. His source is not a comparison to בכור אדם. It is רבא's rule that no valuation is less than a שקל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the background to step 32. There, רבי יהודה was said to agree with רבי יוסי בר יהודה, and the donkey was worth just a שקל.

phrases.english: Actually, he does not compare them,
as Rava said: The verse says
'And all your valuations shall be with the shekel of the Sanctuary,'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ויקרא, in the section about valuing things given to הקדש.

phrases.english: all valuations that you assess
should not be less than a shekel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לָא מַקֵּישׁ, אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 36 by taking the 'no comparison' option and giving a separate source for the שקל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives an independent source from a פסוק and rejects the הקש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A minimum of a שקל seemed to have no source unless one used the הקש, and the הקש would give five.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שקל minimum comes from the rule that all valuations are at least a שקל, with no הקש to בכור אדם.

steps.title: The Rabbis begin to explain their view of רבא's verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who argue with רבי יוסי בר יהודה. It begins to explain that 'that' פסוק about the שקל הקודש is used by them for something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן (who say any amount is enough), what do they do with that פסוק? That פסוק... (the explanation continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins to explain how the רבנן deal with the פסוק that רבי יוסי בר יהודה used to require a שקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 37, רבי יוסי בר יהודה learned the minimum of a שקל from 'all your valuations shall be with the שקל הקודש'. The רבנן allow any amount for a פטר חמור, so they must read that פסוק differently. The word 'ההוא' (that one) points back to that פסוק, and the next amud will tell us what the רבנן learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, meaning the majority opinion. Here they are the ones who say a פטר חמור can be redeemed for any amount.
That one. It points back to a פסוק or teaching that was already mentioned.
The holy שקל. This is the unit in the פסוק that רבא used to teach that no valuation may be less than a שקל.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full answer yet. The sentence starting with 'ההוא' finishes on the next amud, so don't look for the רבנן's reading here.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: that [verse]
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quietly asking, 'what do the רבנן do with רבא's פסוק?' 'That' means the שקל הקודש פסוק from the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 37 explained where רבי יוסי בר יהודה gets his שקל from. Now the גמרא asks how the opposing רבנן explain that same פסוק, and it begins to answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins here: the רבנן use 'that' פסוק (the שקל הקודש) for a different teaching. The details come on the next amud.
